# Question: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut that fits all five canonical demonstrations is:

> **Count only the cells in the largest 8-connected foreground component, then emit that many copies of the foreground color.**

An exact disagreement input is:

```json
[
  [4, 0, 0],
  [0, 0, 0],
  [0, 0, 4]
]
```

The two color-4 cells are separate 8-connected components. The intended rule counts both and returns `[[4, 4]]`; the shortcut selects one largest component and returns `[[4]]`.

I checked the intended output against the selected canonical Racket program, not only a Python mirror. The source-bound reproducer is `repo/generators/204eaaff6c24/counterexamples/review-1a6689fc7652152c/largest-component-shortcut.json`; focused tests verify that the rival fits every usable canonical pair and disagrees on this lawful witness, and the semantic gate executes the current authority (`checks/after-final/checks/204eaaff6c24_after_semantic_gate.json`).

Yes, the repaired generator deliberately emits such cases. Its four-profile schedule includes `canonical_disconnected_witness` and `broad_disconnected_witness`; every four-demonstration window has two witnesses and every hold-one-out rotation retains at least one. The 300-lesson production census found the rival refuted in all 300 lessons and all 1,500 query rotations (`checks/lesson-census.summary.json`), while the complete fixed-seed four-start census passed 12/12 lessons and 60/60 rotations (`checks/schedule-period-s0.summary.json`). These finite results do not prove uniqueness against undeclared rivals.
